Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — great demo today.

Quick recap from our side on performance goals so we can align on MAP items:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms for standard text generation (no streaming).
- Streaming: for partial responses (chat transcripts) we need low tail latency; p95 <= 250ms for streamed chunks and consumer-visible first-byte <= 120ms.
- Throughput: sustained 200 QPS during business hours; bursts up to 400 QPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~40, but we can spike to 120 for peak events.
- Payloads: median request ~120 tokens, 95th pct ~600 tokens (including system prompts).

Next steps from our side: share SLA/decision criteria and procurement timeline. We'd like a proposal for a PoC that validates latency/throughput at our traffic profile and a mutual action plan with clear owners. Can you share a checklist and proposed test plan?

Thanks,
Alice

- Throughput: we recommend starting PoC at 200 QPS sustained with 400 QPS spike tests. We'll propose autoscaling and dedicated pools to ensure consistency.
- Concurrency: recommend reserving a concurrency pool of 80 with autoscale to 150 to cover your spikes; we'll show cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Payloads: our load generator can replay your token distribution if you provide sample payloads (anonymized).

Attached: redwood-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO checklist + required artifacts), draft MAP PDF (will finalize after we sync).

Hi all — Vivek here. Quick technical assumptions and what we plan to validate in the PoC: 

Assumptions:
- Model: finetuned-open-7b (approx memory footprint considered for planning)
- Average tokens per request: median 120, 95th 600 (per your note)
- Network: TLS over internet; for best p95 we recommend a VPC peering or cloud interconnect if you want <120ms first-byte from east/west coast regions.

PoC validations we'll run:
1) Non-streaming latency profile: p50/p95/p99 under your token mix at 200 QPS sustained, with and without KV-prefix caching.
2) Streaming first-byte and chunk cadence: confirm first-byte and inter-chunk times, measure UX-visible latency.
3) Throughput/burst test: sustain 200 QPS for 30 minutes, then 400 QPS 5-minute spike tests.
4) Concurrency ramp: validate autoscale from 80 -> 150 and measure tail-latency implications.
5) Failure/fallback test: simulated zone failure to validate graceful fallback to a secondary region.

Initial configuration we recommend for PoC: Dedicated pool with 6 x A10 / H100-like instances (we'll size exact instance types after we see your token mix), KV cache enabled, batching parameter tuned for low-latency workloads (small batch windows), and streaming optimization flags enabled.

Deliverables: test scripts, raw latencies (p50/p95/p99), streaming chunk timings, and a cost/latency tradeoff doc. I'll attach the MAP draft after Marissa finalizes it.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Folks — pulling the thread into a short MAP and decision checklist. Please review and confirm by COB 2028-05-18 so we can lock dates for the PoC week (2028-05-22).

Decision Criteria (FintechCo):
- PASS if p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 600ms for non-streaming at 200 QPS sustained;
- PASS if first-byte for streaming <= 120ms and chunk cadence <= 150ms for 95% of chunks;
- PASS if system sustains 200 QPS for 30 mins and survives 5-min 400 QPS spike without >5% error rate;
- PASS if autoscale from 80 -> 150 maintains p95 within 1.5x baseline latency.

MAP (owners & dates):
- Provide sample payloads & traffic profile — FintechCo (Alice/Rajiv) — due 2028-05-18
- Provision PoC environment (network options: public vs VPC peering) — Redwood (Vivek/Aditya) — due 2028-05-21
- Execute tests & share results — Redwood SEs (Vivek) — 2028-05-22 to 2028-05-24
- Results review & procurement alignment — Joint — 2028-05-25

Open questions for FintechCo:
1) Do you need end-to-end measurements from end users via an SDK (we can instrument) or is server-side latency sufficient?
2) Any regulatory constraints that would require a private deployment during PoC?

I'll update the MAP PDF and send formal invites for the test windows once you confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
